scope: Conservative exterior candidate for the historic east main building and tall principal clock tower. No whole-site, precise restoration, photo-scale or geographic acceptance.

facts: 南京西路325号; began 1933 and completed 1934.
East building has four floors, locally five; west building three; courtyard basement one.
Text names a principal clock tower and another side clock tower.
source_review.limit: 2018 complex description does not allocate every visible 2013 facade bay, establish uniform storey heights or provide surveyed dimensions.

facts: East-building repair and initial exhibition had reached a trial-opening phase.
West building by 黄陂北路 and intermediate courtyard remained under construction.
source_review.limit: Alteration-period evidence; 2013 roof terrace fixtures are not established as 2018 or 2026 condition.

facts: Secondary narrative describes a body more than 100 m long, four floors, reinforced-concrete structure.
Describes red-brown brick and stone exterior with a colonnade.
Describes an eight-storey principal tower at the northwest corner, 53 m high.
source_review.limit: Current response differs from catalog hash by 30 bytes; the relevant dimensional prose is present. Retain fetched response hash separately. The 53 m datum and endpoint, exact length, and tower floor subdivisions are not surveyed or independently verified.

observations_after_actual_photo_view.observation: A long substantially lower main block extends from the tall tower toward the right of the photo. It has pale stone-like vertical frames and horizontal floor/cornice bands against darker reddish/brown infill. Projecting solid vertical pavilions divide the longer recessed facade stretches.
observations_after_actual_photo_view.modeling_consequence: Retain the elongated body, stronger pavilion divisions and a pale/darker material contrast. Author all dimensions as estimates unless separately anchored.

observations_after_actual_photo_view.observation: A single tall square principal clock tower rises at the near left end. The two visible faces each carry a round light dial inside heavy arched stone-like framing, above long narrow vertical recessed bays. The tower has a projecting lower shoulder with balustrade/cornice bands.
observations_after_actual_photo_view.modeling_consequence: One tall principal tower; do not duplicate it at the opposite body end. Two dial faces are observed; other faces are an explicitly estimated continuation if modeled.

observations_after_actual_photo_view.observation: Above the clocks is a narrower open pavilion/lantern, with tall dark gaps between pale columns and a short balustrade. A red tiled pyramidal/hipped roof with pronounced eaves caps it. A fine finial/pole is visible but its height-datum relation is unknown.
observations_after_actual_photo_view.modeling_consequence: Use actual open space in the lantern and an overhanging hipped cap. Do not use a glazed closed cube, generic flat top or the flagpole as a height control.

observations_after_actual_photo_view.confidence: high overall form; exact grid unverified
observations_after_actual_photo_view.observation: The long facade contains deep dark open colonnade/loggia space behind visible pale columns, with long pale floor and railing/parapet bands. A slimmer upper gallery or terrace-front band with reddish vertical members sits above. Trees conceal much of the lowest facade.
observations_after_actual_photo_view.modeling_consequence: Provide recess depth, columns and continuous horizontal gallery bands rather than treating the long front as one coplanar punched-window wall. Exact column count, clear opening widths and floor-to-floor mapping remain authored estimates.

observations_after_actual_photo_view.observation: Solid projecting pale vertical blocks interrupt the long galleries, including a taller central/right pavilion with narrow openings and a low red hipped cap, and a solid capped end block at the far right. A small circular dial-like detail is visible on the central/right pavilion.
observations_after_actual_photo_view.modeling_consequence: The lower solid pavilion rhythm can be represented. This photo alone does not bind the small circular detail to the text-described secondary clock tower or justify a separate tall tower asset.

observations_after_actual_photo_view.confidence: high visible form; hidden intersections unknown
observations_after_actual_photo_view.observation: A long pitched red-tile roof lies toward the rear of the main body. Smaller roofed projecting portions and an open/partly covered terrace sit in front of it. Pergola-like framing, translucent-looking terrace coverings and rooftop equipment are visible in the 2013 view.
observations_after_actual_photo_view.modeling_consequence: Keep the main pitched red roof distinct from the flat open terrace/gallery zone. Simplify or omit period-specific pergola, coverings, restaurant fixtures, rooftop equipment and vegetation. Do not infer the full roof intersection behind occlusions.

exclusions: The curved ICBC block in the immediate foreground is a separate neighbor.
The huge white curved Shanghai Grand Theatre behind the main building is separate.
The lower red-roof block on the right is not independently bound as an included east-building component; exclude it with western buildings/courtyard links until researched separately.
Trees, people, traffic, modern advertising, roof restaurant furniture, temporary canopies and other streetscape features are not required permanent architectural geometry.
Do not assign surrounding high-rises or the whole former racecourse to this asset.

footprint_review.reason: Eight-corner stepped map outline has no separate tower/east/west/courtyard parts, height or floor fields. The approx. 98.45 m map long extent conflicts in scope/endpoints with the secondary more-than-100 m body statement; neither may be silently rescaled or substituted for the other.

limitations: Elevated oblique single photo has no calibrated image-to-metre control; do not derive exact dimensions, angle, column count, clock diameter or precise roof pitch from pixels.
Documentary 53 m is an explicit secondary anchor only. Its endpoint is unspecified; any candidate base-to-cap treatment must be labeled an interpretation.
Four/local-five floors describes the east building in 2018, while eight tower storeys comes from a different secondary narrative. Neither requires equally spaced windows or uniform heights.
Photo metadata dates the view to 2013-12-22, before 2017-2018 museum alterations. It is not a verified 1934 restoration or 2026 condition.
Full rear/side elevations, hidden lower openings, full footprint, secondary tower boundary and roof/terrace intersections remain unverified.
No geographic registration, historical outside-wall boundary acceptance, city replacement or full listed-place completion follows from this review.
